profile.reading:
This facility in Alpharetta, Georgia, part of the Atlanta metro area, is currently operated by STACK Infrastructure, which identifies it as campus ATL01 on its own website: two buildings, ATL01A at 8 megawatts across 105,000 square feet and ATL01B at 12 megawatts across 133,000 square feet, together totaling 20 megawatts of IT capacity across 238,000 square feet on 18 acres, explicitly stated by STACK to be powered by Georgia Power. The underlying source data for this record carries the name "T5 Data Center," which does not appear anywhere on STACK's current site for this or any other location. T5 Data Centers is a real, separate, currently operating data center developer, confirmed via its own website, claiming more than 3 gigawatts of managed power capacity across facilities it has developed since roughly 2008, but T5's own current site makes no claim to any Alpharetta property. The most plausible explanation for the name/operator mismatch in this record is that T5 originally developed this building before it came under STACK's current ownership or operation, a common pattern in the data center industry where map and property records retain a legacy developer's name after an ownership change, but that specific lineage could not be independently confirmed from any source reached this session, and is flagged here as an open question rather than asserted as settled fact. Alpharetta itself is an established secondary Atlanta-area technology and telecom corridor. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities at ATL01 are not publicly disclosed, and no street address or year of completion is stated on STACK's public site for this campus.

T5 Data Centers, the name attached to this OSM record, describes itself as a developer with more than 3 gigawatts of managed power capacity and roughly 4 million square feet developed across 22 data centers since its founding around 2008, and disclosed in a September 2, 2026 announcement that its construction business is being spun off as an independent entity called EverOn DCS while its operations business transitions to a company called Salute, a corporate restructuring unrelated to this specific Alpharetta building but relevant to understanding T5's current status as a company.

T5 Data Centers is confirmed via its own website (t5datacenters.com) to be a separate, real, currently operating company (3+ GW managed capacity claimed, founded circa 2008), whose own site makes no current claim to any Alpharetta asset. A T5-built-then-STACK-acquired lineage for this specific building is a plausible explanation for the "name vs operator" mismatch in the source OSM data (a common real-estate pattern where the original developer's name persists as a map label after a change of operator) but could NOT be independently confirmed this session -- flagged honestly rather than asserted as fact. reading.body:
T5 Data Center in Alpharetta is operated by Stack Infrastructure following the company's 2019 acquisition from T5 Data Centers. The facility was constructed in 2012 using proceeds from Fulton County Development Authority bonds and established T5's first metro Atlanta presence. Current operator, address, and ownership succession are verified.

Published specifications for this campus are not included in the data provided. Without IT load, total power allocation, or rack count from Stack Infrastructure's spec page, translation into accelerator density or training capacity cannot be performed.

Georgia has 33 mapped data center facilities and 66.3 megawatts of published capacity across four sites with disclosed power figures. T5 Alpharetta ranks fifth among published facilities in the state, indicating it either publishes no power specification or does not appear in the four disclosed figures. Its position in state ranking cannot be interpreted without access to the operator's published specifications.
